summary: Add factual tool-adapter record for three.js light units, fog density and tone-mapping exposure

payload.rationale: Mood lighting profiles publish unit-bearing intensities and fog densities; the unit semantics are factual and belong in one sourced record that the creative profiles link to. Each of the three claims quotes only what its documentation page actually states, and the tuned numeric ranges sit in authored defaults rather than in a claim.

summary: Read the DirectionalLight page; it states the parallel-ray idealisation, the position-to-target direction rule and an intensity default of 1, and names no photometric unit for intensity.

payload.locator: class description: "A light that gets emitted in a specific direction. This light will behave as though it is infinitely far away and the rays produced from it are all parallel."; "its direction is calculated as pointing from the light's position to the DirectionalLight.target position"; "For the target's position to be changed to anything other than the default, it must be added to the scene."; intensity: "The light's strength/intensity." "Default is 1."
payload.source_version: Unversioned official web documentation read 2026-09-07; verify against the installed package version before implementation.

summary: Read the PointLight page; intensity is stated in candela with default 1, power in lumens coupled to intensity, and decay default 2.

payload.locator: class description: "A light that gets emitted from a single point in all directions. A common use case for this is to replicate the light emitted from a bare lightbulb."; intensity: "The light's strength/intensity measured in candela (cd). Default is 1."; power: "Power is the luminous power of the light measured in lumens (lm). Changing the power will also change the light's intensity."; decay: "The amount the light dims along the distance of the light. In context of physically-correct rendering the default value should not be changed. Default is 2."
payload.source_version: Unversioned official web documentation read 2026-09-08; verify against the installed package version before implementation.

summary: Read the FogExp2 page; it describes the falloff qualitatively and gives density default 0.00025. No shading formula is printed on the page.

payload.locator: class description: "This class can be used to define an exponential squared fog, which gives a clear view near the camera and a faster than exponentially densening fog farther from the camera."; density: "Defines how fast the fog will grow dense. Default is 0.00025."
payload.source_version: Unversioned official web documentation read 2026-09-08; verify against the installed package version before implementation.
